column1: Snakes and Ladders — n×n board numbered 1..n² in boustrophedon (zigzag) order; from cell 1, return min dice rolls to reach n². board[r][c]=-1 means normal; otherwise it's the destination of a snake/ladder. Example: standard board with a few snakes/ladders.
column2: PATTERN: BFS over cell numbers. | INSIGHT: From cell c, neighbors are c+1..c+6; if landing cell has a snake/ladder, jump to its destination instead. | STEPS: 1) Helper to convert cell number → (r,c) honoring zigzag. 2) BFS from 1; visited set; pop cell, try +1..+6, resolve snake/ladder if any, enqueue if unvisited. Track distance per layer. 3) Return distance to n² or -1. | TIME/SPACE: O(n²) / O(n²). | PITFALL: The boustrophedon (zigzag) numbering is easy to get wrong — write a tiny conversion helper.

column1: Minimum Genetic Mutation — start gene string of length 8 (chars ACGT), end gene, and a `bank` of valid intermediate genes; return min single-char mutations to reach end (each intermediate must be in bank). Example: start='AACCGGTT', end='AACCGGTA', bank=['AACCGGTA'] → 1.
column2: PATTERN: BFS over strings. | INSIGHT: Same as Word Ladder — neighbors are strings differing by 1 char that exist in bank. | STEPS: 1) bank_set=set(bank); if end not in bank_set: return -1. 2) BFS from start with distance tracking. For each popped gene, generate all 1-char mutations (8·4 candidates); enqueue any in bank_set and not visited. 3) Return distance[end] or -1. | TIME/SPACE: O(N·L·4) / O(N). | PITFALL: Length is fixed at 8, so brute neighbor generation is fine.

column1: Word Ladder — given beginWord, endWord, wordList; return length of the shortest transformation sequence (each step changes exactly one letter; intermediate must be in list); 0 if none. Example: begin='hit', end='cog', list=['hot','dot','dog','lot','log','cog'] → 5.
column2: PATTERN: BFS with pattern preprocessing. | INSIGHT: Build a pattern map where each word indexes into all its single-wildcard versions ('h*t' → ['hot','hat',...]); BFS uses pattern map to find neighbors in O(L) per word. | STEPS: 1) Build pattern_map: for each word, for each i: key=word[:i]+'*'+word[i+1:]; pattern_map[key].append(word). 2) BFS from beginWord; dist=1; pop word; for each pattern key, for each neighbor, if unvisited and == endWord return dist+1, else enqueue. | TIME/SPACE: O(N·L²) / O(N·L²). | PITFALL: Bidirectional BFS roughly halves the search for huge dictionaries.
